rules.label: Restrict processing on an Article 18(1) ground
rules.summary: On the data subject's request, the controller must mark data as restricted when accuracy is contested, processing is unlawful but erasure is opposed, the data is needed by the subject for legal claims, or an Art 21(1) objection is pending verification.
rules.quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller restriction of processing where one of the following applies

rules.label: Restricted data: storage only, other processing only on a stated exception
rules.summary: Once restricted, data may be stored but otherwise processed only with the subject's consent, for legal claims, to protect another person's rights, or for important Union/Member State public interest.
rules.quote: with the exception of storage, only be processed with the data subject's consent or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims

rules.label: Inform the subject before lifting a restriction
rules.summary: A subject who obtained a restriction must be told by the controller before that restriction is lifted.
rules.quote: shall be informed by the controller before the restriction of processing is lifted

rules.label: Notify recipients of rectification, erasure or restriction; name recipients on request
rules.summary: After a rectification, Art 17(1) erasure or restriction, the controller tells every recipient the data was disclosed to unless impossible or disproportionate. It must name those recipients to the subject on request.
rules.quote: to each recipient to whom the personal data have been disclosed, unless this proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort

rules.label: Provide portable data when the portability conditions hold
rules.summary: Data the subject provided, processed by automated means on consent or contract, must be given to the subject in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format. Portability does not by itself erase data and does not cover public-task processing.
rules.quote: which he or she has provided to a controller, in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format

rules.label: Direct controller-to-controller transmission while protecting others
rules.summary: On the subject's request, portable data is sent directly to another controller where technically feasible. Exercising portability must not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.
rules.quote: the right to have the personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another, where technically feasible

rules.label: Stop public-task or legitimate-interest processing after an objection unless overriding grounds
rules.summary: When a subject objects on grounds of their particular situation to processing based on Art 6(1)(e) or (f), including profiling, the controller must stop. The exceptions are demonstrated compelling legitimate grounds that override the subject's interests, or legal claims.
rules.quote: The controller shall no longer process the personal data unless the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds for the processing

rules.label: Stop direct marketing and related profiling on objection, with no override
rules.summary: A subject may object at any time to direct marketing, including related profiling; the data must then no longer be processed for that purpose. No balancing or override is available.
rules.quote: Where the data subject objects to processing for direct marketing purposes, the personal data shall no longer be processed for such purposes.

rules.label: Present the objection right at first communication; automated and research objections
rules.summary: The objection rights must be shown explicitly, clearly and separately no later than the first communication, and in information-society services may be exercised by automated technical means. For Art 89(1) research or statistics, the subject may object unless the processing is necessary for a public-interest task.
rules.quote: shall be explicitly brought to the attention of the data subject and shall be presented clearly and separately from any other information

rules.label: No solely automated decision with legal or similarly significant effects by default
rules.summary: A subject must not be subjected to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that has legal or similarly significant effects, unless an Art 22(2) exception applies.
rules.quote: the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects concerning him or her

rules.label: Use an automated-decision exception only with its condition and safeguards
rules.summary: Solely automated significant decisions are permitted only when necessary for a contract, authorised by law with safeguards, or based on explicit consent. For the contract and consent cases the controller must offer at least human intervention, a chance to give a view, and a way to contest.
rules.quote: the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller, to express his or her point of view and to contest the decision

rules.label: No special-category data in automated decisions unless Art 9(2)(a)/(g) and safeguards
rules.summary: Excepted automated decisions must not rely on special-category data unless explicit consent (9(2)(a)) or a substantial-public-interest law (9(2)(g)) applies and suitable safeguards are in place.
rules.quote: shall not be based on special categories of personal data referred to in Article 9(1), unless point (a) or (g) of Article 9(2) applies

rules.label: Restrict a subject right only under a supplied legislative measure
rules.summary: Rights and obligations in Arts 12-22 and 34 may be limited only by a Union or Member State legislative measure that pursues a listed objective, is necessary and proportionate, and contains the Art 23(2) provisions. Without such a supplied measure the agent must apply the rights normally.
rules.quote: may restrict by way of a legislative measure the scope of the obligations and rights provided for in Articles 12 to 22 and Article 34

rules.label: Preserve complaint, judicial-remedy and representation paths
rules.summary: Subjects may complain to a supervisory authority, seek a judicial remedy against the controller or processor, and mandate a qualifying not-for-profit body to act for them. The agent must describe these routes accurately and never obstruct or condition them.
rules.quote: every data subject shall have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority

decision_paths.situation: An authenticated customer says a late-payment flag on their account is wrong and asks that it not be used while the controller checks. The flag was shared with a collection agency.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the flag is restricted while it is checked and that the customer will be told before the restriction is lifted.

decision_paths.situation: A subject finds that their phone number was collected with no lawful basis. They say: do not delete it, I want it kept as evidence, but stop using it.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm restriction instead of erasure; do not insist the data must be deleted.

decision_paths.situation: A former customer's delivery logs have reached the end of their retention period and are queued for deletion. The customer asks for them to be kept because they need them for a lawsuit against a courier.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the logs are kept restricted, not deleted, and not used for anything else.

decision_paths.situation: Citing personal safety, a customer objects to the controller's legitimate-interest location analytics and asks that it stop while the objection is assessed. No decision on overriding grounds has been made.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the objection is recorded and the analytics processing is restricted pending the assessment.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks to 'freeze' processing of their active-order data because they dislike the company. They do not dispute accuracy, the contract-based processing is lawful and still needed, and no Art 21(1) objection is available.
decision_paths.communication: Within one month, explain that no Art 18(1) ground applies, and state the right to complain to a supervisory authority and to seek a judicial remedy.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing asks the agent to export all customers for a loyalty campaign. One customer's record is restricted under Art 18(1)(a), and they have not consented to other use.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the requesting team the record is excluded because it is restricted.

decision_paths.situation: A subject whose data is restricted has sued the controller. The legal team asks for the restricted records to prepare the defence.
decision_paths.communication: None to the subject; the restriction stays in place for all other uses.

decision_paths.situation: A customer's address is restricted pending an accuracy check. The customer asks the controller to ship an already-paid order to that address anyway.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the address is used only for this shipment and stays restricted otherwise.

decision_paths.situation: A data engineer asks whether restricted records must be purged from the encrypted backup store, where they are only kept and not otherwise used.
decision_paths.communication: Storage of restricted data is permitted; it must not be used for anything else.

decision_paths.situation: The insurer of a third party injured in an incident involving the subject asks for the subject's restricted contact and incident records. It says it needs them to protect its client's rights.
decision_paths.communication: Do not confirm or release anything to the insurer pending the DPO's decision.

decision_paths.situation: A public health body asks for restricted records, citing an important public interest under national law that is not in the scenario policy.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge the request without releasing data; the DPO assesses the claimed legal basis.

decision_paths.situation: Verification shows that the contested address was correct. The operator wants to lift the 18(1)(a) restriction and resume normal use.
decision_paths.communication: Before lifting, tell the subject that verification found the data accurate and that the restriction will end.

decision_paths.situation: Two days into an accuracy dispute, a sales lead asks the agent to lift the restriction now so the record can be used in a campaign. The accuracy check is not finished.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the sales lead the restriction stays until verification is complete and the subject has been informed.

decision_paths.situation: A product manager says the company's fraud-analytics interest clearly outweighs a pending Art 21(1) objection and asks the agent to lift the 18(1)(d) restriction. No verification has been documented.
decision_paths.communication: If the DPO later confirms overriding grounds, the subject must be informed before the restriction is lifted.

decision_paths.situation: After erasing a subject's account data under Art 17(1)(b), the agent sees in the disclosure log that the data was shared with a delivery partner and a payments provider.
decision_paths.communication: Tell each recipient about the erasure.

decision_paths.situation: After a misspelled name and a wrong date of birth are rectified, the subject asks which organisations received the old data.
decision_paths.communication: Name the recipients to the subject and confirm that they were told about the correction.

decision_paths.situation: After a restriction, one of three past recipients turns out to be a dissolved company with no remaining contact point. The other two can be reached.
decision_paths.communication: Notify the two reachable recipients and record why the dissolved one could not be notified.

decision_paths.situation: A subject insists the controller tell its partners that their income figure is wrong. The controller verified the figure as accurate and made no rectification.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that no rectification was carried out, so there is nothing to communicate under Art 19. Give the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: After an erasure, the disclosure log shows the record was syndicated to several thousand affiliate merchants over five years, with no maintained contact list.
decision_paths.communication: Do not tell the subject that recipients were notified until the DPO has decided the scope.

decision_paths.situation: A subject asks for the list of recipients. The disclosure log includes a tax authority that obtained the data in a specific inquiry, and the scenario policy does not say which national law governed it.
decision_paths.communication: List the ordinary recipients. Do not reveal the authority's inquiry entry until the DPO decides.

decision_paths.situation: An authenticated customer asks for a machine-readable copy of the profile details and order history they entered in the app. The processing is contract-based and held in a database.
decision_paths.communication: Provide the data free of charge in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for portability of identity-verification records that the controller keeps to meet a legal obligation (Art 6(1)(c)).
decision_paths.communication: Explain that portability does not cover data processed on this basis and that the access right still applies. Give the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for portability of the creditworthiness score and churn prediction that the controller computed about them.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that the computed scores were not provided by the subject, so Art 20 does not cover them. Access under Art 15 may still be requested.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for portability of handwritten paper complaint forms kept in a physical archive and never digitised.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that portability covers only processing carried out by automated means. Give the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A customer exports their playlist data to move to a competitor but says nothing about closing the account. An operator suggests deleting the account once the export is sent.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the export. Do not imply the account will be deleted unless the subject asks for erasure.

decision_paths.situation: An authenticated customer asks the controller to send their portable account data directly to a named new provider through the supported transfer connector.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm what was sent and to which controller.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for direct transmission to a small provider that has no import interface or other technical channel the controller can use.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that direct transmission is not technically feasible, and give the subject the portable export instead.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks for a portable export of a shared household account that also holds two other adults' order histories and payment notes.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that other account members' data was withheld to protect their rights.

decision_paths.situation: A competitor emails saying it is a customer's new provider and asks the controller to transfer the customer's data to it. There is no instruction from the customer.
decision_paths.communication: Do not confirm whether the person is a customer. A transfer can be made only on the data subject's own verified request.

decision_paths.situation: A customer asks the controller to transmit their uploaded contact book, with thousands of other people's names and numbers, directly to a new marketing platform.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the customer the request is being reviewed because it includes other people's data.

decision_paths.situation: A customer who is a domestic-abuse survivor objects to the controller's legitimate-interest analytics, which track her location in its stores. No compelling grounds or legal-claims need is documented.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm the analytics processing of her data has stopped.

decision_paths.situation: A customer objects on particular-situation grounds to legitimate-interest fraud scoring. The fraud team asserts compelling grounds, but nothing has been demonstrated or documented.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the customer the objection is recorded and processing is restricted while it is assessed.

decision_paths.situation: A customer who is suing the controller objects to it keeping and using the dispute records. The controller's documented assessment shows the records are needed to defend the claim.
decision_paths.communication: Within one month, give the reason (legal-claims ground) and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A customer objects under Art 21(1) to processing of the delivery address needed to fulfil their current order, which is contract-based.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that Art 21(1) does not cover contract-based processing. Give the reasons and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: A customer replies to a promotional email: 'stop sending me marketing'.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that marketing has stopped. Do not ask for reasons or proof; none is needed for a marketing objection.

decision_paths.situation: After a customer objects to marketing, the marketing lead tells the agent to keep them in campaigns because the company's retention-marketing interest is 'compelling'.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the marketing lead that no override exists for direct-marketing objections.

decision_paths.situation: A customer objects to marketing. The agent must decide whether this also stops order confirmations, delivery updates and payment processing on their active orders.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that marketing has stopped and that service messages needed for the contract continue.

decision_paths.situation: A customer has objected to marketing, but the personalisation engine still builds a 'propensity to buy' profile that is used only to target offers.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that marketing-related profiling has also stopped.

decision_paths.situation: The agent works for an email-delivery processor. A recipient of a client's campaign replies to the processor directly, objecting to further marketing.
decision_paths.communication: Pass the objection to the controller without delay so it can stop the marketing; the processor does not decide the request itself.

decision_paths.situation: The agent drafts the first email to a newly registered customer whose data will be processed on legitimate interests for marketing and analytics.
decision_paths.communication: State the right to object, including to direct marketing, explicitly, clearly and separately from other information.

decision_paths.situation: Marketing asks the agent to send the welcome campaign now and mention the objection right only inside the linked terms and conditions.
decision_paths.communication: The campaign cannot go out as drafted. The objection right must appear explicitly and separately in this first communication.

decision_paths.situation: A website visitor's browser sends a standardised machine-readable opt-out signal objecting to the controller's marketing profiling on its online service.
decision_paths.communication: No extra confirmation or form is required from the visitor to make the objection effective.

decision_paths.situation: Citing their particular situation, a customer objects to a private company's Art 89(1) statistical study that uses their purchase data. The study is not a public-interest task.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that their data is excluded from the study going forward.

decision_paths.situation: A subject objects to inclusion in a disease-registry study. The scenario overlay establishes the study as a task carried out for reasons of public interest under Member State law.
decision_paths.communication: Give the reason (public-interest task) and the complaint and judicial-remedy options.

decision_paths.situation: Operations asks the agent to run a job that automatically and permanently bans customers whose behavioural risk score passes a threshold, with no human review. The basis is legitimate interests; there is no explicit consent and no authorising law.
decision_paths.communication: Tell operations that bans must be decided by a person reviewing each case.

decision_paths.situation: The help-centre engine automatically chooses the order in which support articles are shown to each user.
decision_paths.communication: None required.

decision_paths.situation: Before account limits are set, a credit officer reviews each model recommendation, sees the underlying data, and regularly overturns it.
decision_paths.communication: None required beyond the usual decision notice.

decision_paths.situation: A reviewer bulk-approves every model rejection without looking at the cases. The team says this means the decisions are not solely automated.
decision_paths.communication: Do not describe these decisions to subjects as human-reviewed pending the DPO's view.

decision_paths.situation: An applicant requests an instant online credit line. The automated decision is necessary to enter the contract, and human intervention, a way to give a view, and a contest route are all offered.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the applicant how to obtain human intervention, give their view, and contest the decision.

decision_paths.situation: An applicant rejected by the automated credit decision asks for a person to review it and wants to explain that the income data used was out of date.
decision_paths.communication: Do not say the automated decision is final. Confirm a person will review it, taking the applicant's input into account.

decision_paths.situation: Product asks the agent to switch on automated rejection of loan top-up requests based on customers' explicit consent. There is no channel for human intervention, giving a view, or contesting the decision.
decision_paths.communication: Tell product that the automated decisions cannot start until the Art 22(3) safeguards exist.

decision_paths.situation: The team relies on 'consent' for automated loan rejections, but the only evidence is a pre-ticked box in the general terms. No other Art 22(2) ground is claimed.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that a pre-ticked box in the terms is not the explicit consent Art 22(2)(c) requires.

decision_paths.situation: Compliance says a national anti-fraud statute authorises fully automated blocking of suspicious transfers. The statute and its safeguards are not in the scenario policy.
decision_paths.communication: Do not rely on the claimed statute until it is confirmed and supplied.

decision_paths.situation: An automated life-insurance pricing decision, necessary for the contract the applicant requested, would use their health-questionnaire answers. There is no explicit consent for that use and no authorising law.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the requester that the decision cannot be automated using the health data without explicit consent.

decision_paths.situation: Same pricing decision, but the applicant explicitly consented to the health data being used for it, and human intervention, a way to give a view, and a contest route are in place.
decision_paths.communication: Tell the applicant how to obtain human intervention, give their view, and contest the decision.

decision_paths.situation: A team cites a national substantial-public-interest law to justify fully automated eligibility decisions using applicants' health data. The law is not in the scenario policy.
decision_paths.communication: Do not run the automated decisions until the DPO confirms the legal basis and safeguards.

decision_paths.situation: The scenario overlay supplies a Member State statute that restricts the access right for records in an active criminal-fraud investigation file. It also provides that informing the subject would prejudice the investigation. The subject asks for access to that file.
decision_paths.communication: Follow the overlay's notice rule and do not reveal the investigation.

decision_paths.situation: An account manager tells the agent to refuse all of a customer's GDPR requests while the customer's lawsuit against the company is pending. The scenario policy supplies no Art 23 measure. The customer has asked to restrict data they say is inaccurate.
decision_paths.communication: Handle the restriction request normally; a pending dispute alone does not suspend the subject's rights.

decision_paths.situation: An unverified email signed as a police officer asks the controller to ignore a subject's erasure request and not tell them, citing a statute that is not in the scenario policy.
decision_paths.communication: Send no data to the sender. The Art 12(3) response deadline for the subject keeps running while the DPO decides.

decision_paths.situation: The supplied overlay restricts only the access right for an investigation file. The same subject objects to direct marketing.
decision_paths.communication: Confirm that marketing has stopped; do not mention the unrelated restriction.

decision_paths.situation: A subject unhappy with how their erasure request was handled asks how to complain. A team-lead note tells agents to say customers must finish the internal appeal first.
decision_paths.communication: Say they may complain to a supervisory authority (in particular where they live, work, or where the infringement occurred) and seek a judicial remedy against the controller. Do not say an internal appeal must come first.

decision_paths.situation: A frustrated subject asks the agent to file a complaint against the controller with the supervisory authority on their behalf.
decision_paths.communication: Explain that the subject, or a not-for-profit body they mandate under Art 80, lodges the complaint, and how to do it. Do not discourage it.

decision_paths.situation: A caller says they represent a data-rights association mandated under Art 80 and asks for a named customer's account data and complaint history. They give no evidence of a mandate.
decision_paths.communication: Do not confirm whether the person is a customer. Explain what evidence of the mandate is needed.

decision_paths.situation: A not-for-profit data-protection association shows a signed mandate from the subject and statutes proving it is properly constituted. It announces court proceedings against the controller over the subject's refused erasure request.
decision_paths.communication: Acknowledge receipt. Do not dispute the association's standing or discourage the proceedings.

decision_paths.situation: An association with no mandate from the subject says national law lets it bring proceedings over the controller's processing on its own initiative, and asks for the subject's records.
decision_paths.communication: Release no subject data; the claimed national-law standing is assessed by the controller.

open_questions: Art 18(1)(b) vs 17(1)(d): it is unclear whether a subject's choice of restriction over erasure displaces the controller's own obligation to erase unlawfully processed data. Modelled as tension_with DR-04, with restriction as the path outcome.

Art 18(1) is a right the subject must 'obtain' (request), yet 21(1) says processing stops unless grounds are demonstrated. Whether the controller must restrict automatically on any 21(1) objection, or only when asked, is not stated. DP.DR-13.02 restricts proactively.

Art 18(1)(a)/(d) give no time limit for the verification period, and Arts 18/21 set no deadline for the restriction or stop itself. Timing is modelled via 12(3) (without undue delay / one month), which strictly governs 'information on action taken'.

Art 19 covers erasure 'in accordance with Article 17(1)' only. Whether erasure for other reasons (e.g., routine retention expiry, or erasure under 17(2)) also triggers recipient notification is not stated.

Art 19 'impossible or disproportionate effort' has no criteria in the text, and the recipient-list duty has no explicit deadline beyond 12(3). Disproportionate-effort judgments are modelled as ESCALATE to the DPO.

Art 4(9) excludes public authorities receiving data in a particular inquiry from 'recipients'. Whether such entries must be withheld from the Art 19 recipient list depends on the governing Union/Member State law (overlay).
Art 20(1) 'provided by' the subject: the text clearly excludes controller-computed inferences. Whether observed data (activity logs, telemetry) counts as 'provided' is not settled by the text.
Art 20(3)'s public-task exclusion largely overlaps 20(1)(a), since public-task processing is not consent or contract. It is kept as a separate exception node.
Art 20(4) 'shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others' gives no method. Redaction is modelled for clear co-holder data, and ESCALATE for bulk third-party datasets.
Art 21(1) does not say who decides, or by what test, whether 'compelling legitimate grounds' override. It is modelled as a DPO decision; an operational agent should not self-certify it.
Art 21(5) names no technical specification, so which machine-readable opt-out signals count as a valid objection is not determinable from the text.
Art 21(6) together with Art 89(2): Member State law may derogate from Art 21 for research. No such overlay is assumed; DP.DR-15.04 assumes none exists.
Art 22(1) 'solely' and 'similarly significantly affects' are undefined. Token or rubber-stamp human review is modelled as ESCALATE (DP.DR-16.04) because the text does not resolve it.
Art 22(2)(a) 'necessary' for a contract has no test. Paths assert necessity as a scenario fact rather than deriving it.
Art 22(4): whether decisions using proxies or inferences for special-category data (e.g., inferred health status) are 'based on' Art 9(1) data is not addressed.
Art 22(4) via 9(2)(a): explicit consent may be unavailable where Union or Member State law says the prohibition cannot be lifted. DP.DR-18.02 assumes no such law.

Art 80(1) covers lodging complaints and Arts 77-79/82 remedies. It does not say whether a mandated body may exercise Arts 15-22 rights for the subject, or how a controller verifies a mandate. DP.OL-03.03 and DP.OL-03.04 assume disclosure needs separate verification and controller sign-off.

Art 23: a supplied measure may also restrict Art 12(4) refusal reasons and remedy notices (Art 23 covers Art 12). The communication content in restricted cases therefore depends entirely on the overlay text.
Art 78(2) gives the supervisory authority a three-month progress-reporting duty. It binds the authority, not the controller, so no controller deadline node was created.
